items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the civil service law, in relation to certain reports relating
to health benefits for state and retired state employees
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S4097

SPONSOR: GOUNARDES
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the civil service law, in relation to certain reports
relating to health benefits for state and retired state employees

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

Requires New York State health benefit plan hospital pricing report to
increase transparency and evidence-based decisions concerning the NYSHIP
benefit through an analysis of the healthcare expenses, trends and the
range of variables that influence health care spending, in particular,
hospital costs.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section one of the bill would amend the Civil Service Law to require the
Department of Civil Service to conduct a hospital pricing report and
make such report publicly available. The report shall include a compar-
ative analysis of hospital prices based on the following service catego-
ries:(i) inpatient hospital, (ii) outpatient hospital, and (iii) emer-
gency room services. The report shall compare the prices to the process
for similar services reimbursed under title eighteen of the Social Secu-
rity Act. Such a report shall also include a comprehensive analysis of
the prior five years of hospital prices and expenditures to establish
trends in hospital prices and total expenditures.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

The New York State Health Insurance Programs (NYSHIP) was established in
1957 for State employees and a year later included local governments and
school districts. Today, NYSHIP is one of the largest public employer
health insurance programs in the country, insuring over 1.2 million
active government employees, retirees and their families. This NYSHIP
benefit is a key component of state employment benefits and in the
aggregate, has the ability to affect the state's fiscal health. It is
critical that state policymakers who make decisions regarding the admin-
istration of the benefit make evidence-based decisions concerning the
benefit through an analysis of the healthcare expenses, trends and the
range of variables that influence health care spending, in particular,
hospital costs. Variation in hospital pricing has an impact on premiums,
and ultimately an impact on both the public employees and the state's
fiscal plan.

The state has little control over the price differences in hospitals.
How the state's taxpayers' dollars are being spent on these services is
also opaque. Media reports have highlighted the wild fluctuations in
hospital prices for many routine procedures among large hospital
systems. These fluctuations are not rooted in any apparent justification
based on quality or outcomes. A recent 32BJ Health Fund revealed that it
paid private hospital systems more than 300% of Medicare rates.

Understanding the underlying cost drivers in providing hospital services
is an important aspect of providing NYSHIP benefits for valued NYS
public employees. The state should take advantage of its access to data
on expenditures made for hospital services for NYSHIP beneficiaries.
This data should be routinely analyzed to determine what factors influ-
ence state spending for its covered employees. This analysis can then be
used to provide the solid base for any future decision-making. An
updated annual analysis can provide the transparency and visibility into
this system that is needed to ensure that NYSHIP continues to be fiscal-
ly strong and taxpayer dollars are spent prudently.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

This is a new bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This bill is effective immediately.

approvalMessage.text:
APPROVAL MEMORANDUM - No. 48 Chapter 703
 
       MEMORANDUM filed with Senate Bill Number 4097-B, entitled:
 
    "AN  ACT  to  amend  the  civil  service law, in relation to certain
        reports relating to health benefits for state and retired  state
        employees"
 
    APPROVED
 
  This  bill  amends  the Civil Service Law to require the Department of
Civil Service (DCS) to collect and analyze health care  claims  data  to
develop  and  publish  a  report  on hospital pricing for New York State
health benefit plans. The bill requires DCS  to  collect  health  claims
data  from  health  insurers and health maintenance organizations (HMOs)
related to rates and hospital service usage by current and retired state
employees and their dependents. The bill requires a comparative analysis
of in-network and out-of-network rates for specified service  categories
for the prior five years. The bill would become effective immediately.
 
  I  support the goals of this bill, and recognize the value of increas-
ing transparency in hospital pricing. However, as drafted, the bill does
not consider data access issues related to  obtaining  information  from
third-party  commercial insurers. DCS, as the State agency that adminis-
ters the New York State Health Insurance Plan, only has access to claims
data related to the State's self-funded Empire Plan. DCS does  not  have
access  to individual claims data from HMOs. Additionally, the reporting
on certain services categories in the bill is not feasible due to  bill-
ing code limitations. To address these issues, technical and operational
amendments were necessary.
 
  I have reached an agreement with the Legislature to enact these chang-
es.  On the basis of that agreement, I am pleased to sign this bill.

  This bill is approved.                         (signed) KATHY HOCHUL
 
                                ______

summary: Directs the president of the civil service commission to collect health care claims data relating to the price and utilization of hospital benefits by active employees, retired employees and their dependents and to publish a New York State health benefit plan hospital pricing report.
title: Requires New York State health benefit plan hospital pricing report
